pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
Our Commitment to Every Child
The school aim is for all our children to reach their potential, guided by our HEART values:
We ensure that teaching and learning opportunities meet the needs of all our pupils, and that appropriate provision is provided for those who require additional support.
We recognise that there are a number of children who require further support and therefore we allocate additional funding to ensure that we can support all of our most disadvantaged pupils in the most effective way. We also recognise that not all pupils who receive Pupil Premium funding will be socially disadvantaged and that not all pupils who are socially disadvantaged will be eligible for Pupil Premium, and our use of funding represents this.
Achievement
Teamwork
Our Pupil Premium Strategy Statement
As a new school, we are in our first year of operation with only Reception and Year 1 pupils. We will publish our pupil premium strategy statement following our first full academic year.
Our strategy statement will demonstrate how we are using pupil premium funding to:
We will spend the pupil premium on 'evidence-informed' activities chosen from the DfE's 'menu of approaches' The Key Leaders, prioritising high-quality teaching and targeted support that meets the specific needs of our pupils.
As our school grows and we gather data about our pupils' progress and outcomes, we will refine our approach to ensure pupil premium funding has the maximum impact on closing any attainment gaps and supporting every child to thrive.

pageCache.text:
Attendance and Absence
Hounsome Fields Primary School is an inclusive school and we wish for all children to have the best educational experience they can. Regular school attendance is vital to ensure that all children achieve their full potential. Regular attendance serves as a key mechanism to support children’s educational, economic, and social outcomes.
Schools play an essential role in facilitating positive peer relationships, which significantly contribute to better mental health and overall wellbeing. By attending school consistently, children are afforded the opportunity to engage with their classmates, build friendships, and develop essential social skills that are critical to their future success. The relationships formed during these formative years are instrumental in shaping a child's character and resilience.
All children should aim to be in school 100% of the time, as this commitment not only enhances their academic performance but also fosters personal growth and development, pupils who are present in school are more likely to perform well academically, develop a sense of belonging within the school community and feel connected to their peers and teachers, which further supports their emotional and social development.
Learning is a progressive activity; each day’s lessons build upon those of the previous days. Classes also use discussions, demonstrations, experiments and participation as part of the daily learning activities and these cannot be made up by those who are absent.
If a child is frequently absent, they risk falling behind in their learning. This disruption in their education can lead to gaps in knowledge and will hinder their academic progress. Therefore, attendance is fundamentally important in ensuring that young people become successful learners.
Getting your child to school on time matters. It is important that your child arrives to school on time. If they are late and miss the register, it may be recorded as an unauthorised absence. The school gate is open for pupils at 8.15am and registration closes at 8.45am.
5 minutes late each day = 3 days missed from school = 15 missed lessons each year
10 minutes late each day = 6 days missed from school = 30 missed lessons each year
15 minutes late each day = 9 days missed from school = 45 missed lessons each year

Attendance and Absence

SEND
At Hounsome Fields Primary, we are ambitious and hold high expectations for all of our children. We recognise that adaptations are required for some children to achieve progress within our curriculum. High Quality Teaching allows for curriculum adaptations to be made, with all children working on the same skills and towards the same end point.
As a new school with only Year R and Year 1, alongside our SEMH Resourced Provision, we are building our inclusive culture from the foundation. Some children will need help and support throughout their time at school, whilst others will benefit from support for a shorter time. Most additional needs are met by adapted provision within the classroom. Additional, and more personalised provision, is made through a variety of evidence-based interventions.
All teachers at Hounsome Fields Primary are teachers of SEND, and all staff working with children with SEND hold the same high ambitions to deliver adaptive teaching. All staff are responsive and adaptive to what children can do.
Our ambition is holistic, and we recognise the key influences that interactively affect children's learning and development. Through our curriculum and adaptive teaching approach, we support complex everyday activities and interactions with each child's immediate environment.
Our Adaptations
Adaptations may include but are not limited to:
Individualised timetables
The Nest (our SEMH Resourced Provision)
Our SEMH Resourced Provision is an integral part of our school community, providing specialist support for children with social, emotional and mental health needs. Children in the provision benefit from:
There are specialist admissions requirements for The Nest. Children can move flexibly between the resourced provision and mainstream classes based on their individual needs and progress, with the goal of maximising participation in the full school community. Our SENDco is Mr Carter, you can contact him by using the email address: info@hounsomefields.school or by calling the school on 01276 930264.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At EEEA, we create primary curriculums that are designed to inspire and engage our students while adhering to the standards set by the National Curriculum. We believe that a well-rounded education is crucial for developing curious, knowledgeable, and well-prepared individuals. Our curriculum is meticulously crafted to spark a love for learning in every child, encouraging them to explore a wide range of subjects with enthusiasm and confidence.
We set high expectations for both our students and our staff, ensuring that every lesson is delivered with excellence and every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our dedicated teachers employ innovative teaching methods and resources to make learning exciting and relevant, helping students to connect what they learn in the classroom to the world around them. This approach not only enhances academic achievement but also fosters critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills.
By integrating the National Curriculum with our own high standards, we aim to provide a challenging yet supportive learning environment. We continuously assess and refine our curriculum to ensure it meets the evolving needs of our students and society. Our goal is to equip our students with the knowledge, skills, and values they need to succeed in their future endeavors, fostering a lifelong love of learning and a commitment to excellence.

Admissions
If your child was born between 1 September 2021 and 31 August 2022, they will be eligible to start school in the academic year September 2026
At Hounsome Fields Primary School, we strive to provide for your child the best education possible in an excellent learning environment. Our vision and values are growing and developing as the school grows and reflects those within the community. Hounsome Fields Primary School is a safe, happy, respectful environment which aims to combine the life experiences and values of our children and families with the school culture. To achieve this inclusive environment, we respect and value the differences and diversity within our community.
We aim to help children develop their own identity, and create a sense of belonging in an environment which supports their development and prepares them for their lifelong learning journey.
Hounsome Fields Primary School gives all pupils the opportunity to develop enquiring minds, building on their natural curiosity and confidence with an aim of creating positive, respectful relationships which make them feel valued.
We would welcome the opportunity to meet with you and show you around our wonderful school.
Please call our school office to confirm your attendance.
Admissions Timetable:
Deadline for Applications
Notification date for on-time applicants
Waiting list established
Starting School Year R (Reception)
If you're seeking a school placement during the academic year, you'll need to complete an In-Year Application. All such applications are handled by Hampshire County Council, who manage this process on behalf of the school. For more information on school admissions, feel free to contact us on (01276 930 264), and we can discuss your options. Alternatively, you can visit the website provided, which offers details on the application process, guidance information, and a catchment area finder.
https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/admissions/applicationprocess/inyear
A hard copy of this form is available by contacting the school.
Upon receipt of an in-year application, the school will aim to notify the parents of the outcome of their application in writing within 10 school days, but applicants must be notified in writing within 15 school days. Where an application is refused, there is the right to appeal. Details of how to appeal can be found below.
All in-year appeals will be heard within 30 school days.
Where an applicant is offered a school place following an in-year application, and the offer is accepted, arrangements will be made for the child to start school as soon as possible, particularly where the child is out of school.
Parents or guardians who have been denied a school place for their child have the right to appeal the decision. Appeals can be submitted at any time.
The Surrey Appeals Service manages school appeals on our behalf.
https://www9.surreycc.gov.uk/SchoolAdmissionAppeal/School?dfeno=8502070
Parents will first need to create a log in to lodge an appeal using the link above. Please note that because we are not a Surrey school our school information is not on the Surrey website.
